subject: Request: localized reference release (DE/FR/JP) — consent & trademark checks

To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Dubois <claire.dubois@acme-eu.de>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Draft case study — quick follow-up on translations

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the case study draft — the team loved the narrative. We have two asks before we can sign off for publication: 1) localized German and French versions for EU channels (legal needs to confirm trademark phrasing), and 2) a Japanese version for our APAC marketing hub (we work with Kumo in Japan who will manage translation).

Can Redwood provide the translated copy or a translation-ready source (DOCX) and a short consent form for legal to sign? We prefer to review localized drafts prior to public release.

Attached: acme-case-study-en.pdf

Best,
Lena Müller
Head of Marketing, AcmeEU GmbH

Hi Lena — great to hear the team liked it.

We can absolutely provide translation-ready DOCX files and a short customer consent form. I'm looping in Vivek from Partnerships (for JP coordination) and Neha from Legal/Privacy to confirm the exact legal language for EU trademark mentions.

Action items for us:
- Redwood to deliver localized draft files (DE/FR/JP) by EOD Friday 2026-12-04.
- Provide a single-page consent form you can sign and return (PDF).
- Share the translation glossary for product names/trademarks so wording stays consistent.

I'll follow up with the deliverables and a link to a Drive folder.

Thanks — Laura

Redwood Inference | laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -08:00

Hi team,

FYI I reached out to Kenji at Kumo to confirm Japanese proofreading and cultural checks. Kenji said they can review but prefer to receive an English source plus a translation memory/glossary to avoid name mistranslations (particularly for the product marks).

Neha — can you confirm the legal wording we require for EU public references? Specifically: whether we can use the phrase "customer of Redwood Inference" or if Acme needs an approved alternate (e.g., "partner" or "selected customer"). Also, any constraints on logos and trademark adjacent language.

Kenji contact: Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@kumo.co.jp> (copied in next mail).

-Vivek

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 10:45:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Draft case study — quick follow-up on translations

Laura / Vivek —

Short answer: we need explicit written consent for localized variants if they alter substantive claims or include new customer quotes. For styling (logos/trade names) we require:
- a signed consent (I'll provide a single-page PDF template)
- confirmation of exact trade name usage (DE/FR versions must match the registered trademark casing)
- approval for any translated customer quotes — if Acme wants to translate quotes, we need them to confirm wording in the target language.

I've attached the consent template (consent-template.pdf) and a quick checklist for localized releases. I recommend we deliver translation drafts with highlighted strings that change meaning (metrics, quotations).

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
